0.en: On the Difference of the Scene of Death

en: The whole life of the Christian is to be a preparation for this change, his wishes are even directed toward it; daily intercourse with the images of death and with the hopes of that life, compared with which the enjoyments, the joys of this world — to which he does not attach himself and in which, like a stranger, he takes only a weak share — are worth no attention, is to make the leaving of this scene of his activity not only not terrible to him, but even pleasant. — Even less than the moment of death is terrible to him does he dread annihilation, the ceasing of the harmony, as if the instrument were broken, or his future fate — his whole life was a meditatio mortis.
It seems to him only the preparatory school for the future; in itself it has no value, only some value in relation to the future.
What are fifty to eighty years too, spent and used up on that, which measured against boundless eternity, the whole duration of our existence, are only a moment?
Who in sixty years should be able to forget for a moment the terrible alternative: eternal bliss or eternal damnation?

Who, against the ever newly awakening fear of unworthiness for the former, should not flee to the means of grace offered by precisely the doctrine that makes us acquainted with these terrors? who should not [wait] for the moment of this terrible catastrophe, when he not only takes leave of everything that was ever dear to him, but when in a few hours or minutes he will see shining no longer the splendour of this sun, but that of the judgment seat, before which his fate is now decided for eternity? who should not for this moment of anxious expectation gather around himself all the weapons of comfort? who at least should not there, still in haste, like one who [must] suddenly undertake a journey for which he had no time to prepare, pack up more of spiritual equipment, as much as time and his illness allow?

Hence we see the beds of the sick surrounded by clergymen and friends, who groan out to the oppressed soul of the dying man the printed and prescribed sighs; hence we hear that with all reminders and exhortations the refrain forms the close: memento mori; the mightiest of all motives to act are fetched from beyond the grave — [to be able] to die beautifully or piously, to have presence of mind enough to recall now the verses and rhymes learned at school with sweat, and to be able to say them and other things.
zh: 基督徒的整个生活应当是对这一变化的准备，他的愿望甚至就朝着这一点；天天与死的种种形象、与那种生命的种种希望打交道——比起它们来，这个世界的享受和快乐不值一顾，他并不附着于它们，只像一个外人那样沾上一点点——这应当使他对离开自己活动的这个舞台不仅不觉得可怕，甚至觉得愉快。——他对死亡的那一刻不觉得可怕，就更不害怕毁灭，不害怕和声的中止（就好像乐器被打碎了一样），也不害怕自己将来的命运——他整个一生都是一场 meditatio mortis，一场对死亡的默想。
它在他看来只是为将来作准备的学校；它本身没有价值，只有在与将来的关系上才有一点价值。
再说，五十年到八十年又算得了什么？把这些年用在那上面、耗在那上面，而它们比起无限的永恒、比起我们存在的全部延续，不过是一瞬间。
在六十年的岁月里，谁又能有一刻忘掉那个可怕的二选一：永远的至福，还是永远的诅咒？

面对着那种一再新生的、怕自己不配得到至福的恐惧，谁不会逃向种种恩典手段呢——它们正是那门让我们知道这些恐怖的学说所提供的？谁不会去等这场可怕灾难的那一刻呢——那时他不只是告别一切曾经令他珍爱的东西，而且在几个小时或几分钟之后，他再也看不到这个太阳的光辉，而将看到审判宝座的光辉，他的命运此刻就要在它面前永远定下来？谁不会为这个惶惶等待的时刻，把一切安慰的武器都聚到自己身边？谁至少不会在那时还匆匆忙忙，像一个突然[必须]出门旅行、却没时间准备的人那样，尽量把灵性的装备打包带走，能带多少带多少——只要时间和他的病允许？
所以我们看到病人的床前围满了教士和朋友，他们对着垂死的人那憋闷的灵魂，把印好的、规定好的叹息呻吟给他听；所以我们听到，在所有的提醒和劝诫之后，结尾总是那句叠句：memento mori；行动的动机中最有力的那些，都是从坟墓那边取来的：要[能]死得漂亮、死得虔诚，要有足够的清醒，能重新想起当年在学校里流着汗背下来的句子和韵文，并且能念出它们和别的话来。

en: The heroes of all nations die in the same way, for they have lived, and in their life they have learned to acknowledge the power of nature.
But impatience with it, with its petty ills, also makes one unfit to bear its greater effects.

How else could it come about that the peoples in whose religion preparation for death is a main point, a main stone in the whole building, on the whole die so unmanly, whereas other nations see this moment approach unconstrainedly?

As at a meal one man begins early in the morning to have his hair curled, puts on his finery, has his horses harnessed, and, full of the importance of the coming undertaking, ponders the whole time how he should behave, how he should conduct the conversation, and like a young orator is afraid whether he will do his business well24) — while another goes about his business in the morning and only a few minutes before the hour of the table remembers the invitation and steps up to it as plainly and unconstrainedly as if he were at home.

How different the images that have passed from death into the imaginations of our people and of the Greeks — with the latter a beautiful genius, the brother of sleep, immortalised in monuments above the graves; with us the bone-man, whose gruesome skull parades above all coffins.
Death reminded them of the enjoyment of life, us [of] making it distasteful to ourselves; to them it was a savour unto life, to us unto death.

As in respectable society we do not speak of certain natural things, do not even write them, so they circumscribed death, softened its images, which the orators and preachers paint for us in all possible hideous colours in order to strike terror into us and to spoil our enjoyment.
zh: 所有民族的英雄都死得一样，因为他们活过，而且在一生中学会了承认自然的力量。
可是对它不耐烦，对它那些小小的灾祸不耐烦，也会让人没本事承受它更大的作用。
要不然怎么会这样呢：有些民族，在他们的宗教里，对死亡的准备是整座建筑的一个要点、一块主石，可他们总体上却死得那么没有丈夫气；而别的民族反倒能坦然地看着这个时刻临近？
就像赴一场宴席：一个人一大早就让人给他卷头发、穿上华丽的衣服、叫人套好马，满脑子都是这件即将到来的大事，一路上都在琢磨自己该怎么举止、话该怎么讲，还像一个年轻演讲人那样担心自己能不能把事情办好24)；另一个人上午照常办自己的事，直到开饭前几分钟才想起这个邀请，就那么朴素、自在地走过去，好像在自己家里一样。
死亡在我们民族和希腊人的想象里留下的形象，差别有多大——在希腊人那里，是一个美好的精灵，睡眠的兄弟，被永远留在墓上的纪念碑里；在我们这里，却是骷髅人，他那可怕的颅骨在所有棺材上面招摇。
死提醒他们去享受生活，对我们却[提醒我们]把生活弄得倒胃口；对他们，它是使人活的香气，对我们却是使人死的香气。
我们在体面的社交场合不谈某些自然的事情，连写都不写；同样地，他们把死亡绕着说，把它的形象放温和些——而演说家和布道者为了吓唬我们、败掉我们的兴致，却用一切可能的丑恶颜色把这些形象画给我们看。

en: [Three fragments toward a critique of Christianity]
zh: [基督教批判的三个片段]

en: α) By objective religion I understand this whole system of the connection of our duties and wishes with the idea of God and the immortality of the soul — and it is therefore also to be called theology, when this does not occupy itself merely with the cognition of the existence and the properties of God, but does so in relation to men and the needs of their reason.
zh: α) 我把客观宗教理解为这样一个完整的体系：我们的义务和愿望与上帝的观念、与灵魂不死的观念之间的联系——所以它也可以叫作神学，只要神学不只是去认识上帝的存在和属性，而是在与人、与人的理性需要的关联中来做这件事。

en: β) Insofar as this theory does not exist merely in books, but the concepts are grasped by men, the love of duty and the respect for the moral law (insofar as they are strengthened by the idea) are felt, to that extent religion is subjective.

Since now civil legislation has as its immediate purpose not morality but only legality, and since for the furthering of respect for the moral law and of the disposition to fulfil the laws in spirit no special institutions have been made that would have this purpose, but this is regarded as also belonging to religion, we will here too not separate these from one another, but regard as the purpose of religious institutions not merely the furthering of morality through the idea of God, but also of morality in general.
zh: β) 只要这套理论不只是在书里存在，而是被人以概念把握住，对义务的爱和对道德法则的敬重（只要它们被观念所加强）被人感受到，那么宗教就是主观的。
既然民事立法直接的目的不是道德，而只是合法性，而为了促进对道德法则的敬重、促进在精神上履行法律的意向，又没有设立专门以这个为目的的机构，反倒认为这也属于宗教，那么我们也就不在这里把两者分开，而是把宗教机构的目的看作：不仅是通过上帝的观念促进道德，而且是一般地促进道德。

en: γ) Not all drives of human nature, such as that of propagation etc., have morality as their purpose, but the highest purpose of man is morality, and among his dispositions for furthering this, his disposition to religion is one of the most excellent.

The cognition of God cannot by its nature be dead, it has its origin in the moral nature of man, in practical need, and from it morality in turn springs; or if the spread of the name, of the glory of Christ or of Mahomet were its main purpose, then in Greece Orpheus or Homer would deserve to be famous and honoured just as much as Jupiter and Pallas, then it would have cause to be proudest of the Saxon-converter Charles or of proselytising Spaniards in America or of the Jew-hunter Schulz; — or if the glorification of the name of God [were its main purpose], then there would be no better Christians than the hymn-rich Birgitta swallows, and the pope at the great mass in St Peter's would be a worthier object of God's good pleasure than the corporal (Woltemar), who saved thirteen persons from the shipwreck at the sacrifice of his life and died in the service of humanity at the fourteenth.
zh: γ) 人性中并非所有的冲动——比如生殖的冲动等等——都以道德为目的，但人的最高目的是道德，而在人有助益于这一点的各种禀赋里，向宗教的禀赋是最突出的之一。

对上帝的认识按其本性不可能是死的，它起源于人的道德本性，起源于实际的需要，而道德又从它那里产生出来；或者说，如果传扬基督或穆罕默德的名字和荣耀是它的主要目的，那么在希腊，俄耳甫斯或荷马就同样有资格像朱庇特和帕拉斯那样出名、受敬奉，它也就有理由最引以为豪的是感化萨克森人的查理、是在美洲劝人改宗的西班牙人、是专门去找犹太人的舒尔茨；——或者，如果[它的主要目的是]显扬上帝的名字，那就没有比那些歌多得不得了的布里吉特燕子更好的基督徒了，而教皇在圣彼得教堂做大弥撒时，也会比那个下士（沃尔特马尔）更是上帝所喜悦的对象——这下士牺牲自己的性命从海难里救出十三个人，在救第十四个人时死在了为人类服务的事情上。

en: δ) To make objective religion subjective must be the great business of the state; the institutions must be compatible with the freedom of dispositions, must not do violence to conscience and freedom, but work indirectly on the determining grounds of the will — how much can the state do? how much must be left to every man?
zh: δ) 把客观宗教变成主观的，必须是国家的大事；这些机构必须与信念的自由相容，不能对良心和自由施加强制，而要间接地作用于意志的种种规定根据——国家能做多少？又有多少必须留给每个人自己？

en: ε) The furthering of morality, this purpose of religion, happens a) through its doctrines, b) ceremonies.
Every religion has already provided for both and already contains the disposition to both — the state through the constitution, through the spirit of the government.
zh: ε) 促进道德，也就是宗教的这个目的，是通过 a) 它的学说、b) 仪式来实现的。
每一种宗教都已经为这两方面作了安排，也已经含有这两方面的禀赋——国家则通过宪法、通过政府的精神。

en: ζ) To what extent does the Christian religion qualify itself for this?
The Christian religion is originally a private religion, modified according to the needs of the circumstances of its origin, of men and of prejudices:
zh: ζ) 基督教在什么程度上适合做这件事？
基督教最初是一种私人宗教，是按照它产生时的种种情况的需要、按照人和种种成见的需要而改过的：

en: a) its α) practical doctrines are pure and have the good presented mostly in examples — for where, Matth.

5/6 etc., the spirit of morality is presented universally and does not limit itself merely to what is formal but has material precepts, there it is subject to misunderstandings and has also been misunderstood.
zh: a) 它 α) 的实际学说是纯粹的，并且让善大多以例子的方式呈现出来——因为哪里，马太
5/6 等等，道德的精神被普遍地表述出来，不只是局限于形式的东西，而是有实质性的规定，那么它就是会被人误解的，事实上也被人误解过。

en: β) [the] historical truths on which it is built — in them the miraculous is always subject to unbelief; as long as it is private religion, it stands free to everyone to believe them or not, but as public religion there must always be unbelievers.
zh: β）〔那些〕它赖以建立的历史真理——其中的神奇成分总是逃不过不信；只要它是私人宗教，信不信就随每个人的便，可一旦成了公共宗教，就总会有人不信。

en: γ) [in it there is] no provision for the imagination as with the Greeks, it is sad and melancholy — oriental, not grown on our soil, can never assimilate itself to it.
zh: γ）〔它里面〕没有像希腊人那样为想象力作安排，它是哀伤而忧郁的——东方的，不是长在我们土地上的，永远没法跟我们的土地同化。

en: b) The ceremonies, to the purpose as private religion, have entirely lost their sense and spirit since it has become public religion — besides, [they serve] still as means of grace, not wedded to the spirit of cheerfulness — yet since they became public, they could have become promoters of tolerance, if one had not — if one had not with violence bound up with them exclusive hypotheses — now unfortunately distinguishing marks of sects, though they could well have been the opposite.
zh: b）这些仪式，作为私人宗教本来很合用，可一旦它成了公共宗教，就完全失去了自己的意义和精神——此外〔它们〕还充当恩典手段，却没有跟快乐的精神结成一气——不过它们既然公开了，本来是可以成为宽容的推动者的，只要人们不——只要人们不用暴力把排他性的假设一并绑上去——可惜如今却成了各教派的区别标志，而它们本来完全可以起相反的作用。

en: c) other commands with regard to the way of life:
zh: c）关于生活方式的其他诫命：

en: α) withdrawal from public business β) distribution of alms — the piling up of a fortune [is] possible in private religion, not practicable in the state; also [what] otherwise was an act of piety [is] now bound up with public honour.
zh: α）退出公共事务　β）施舍赈济——积攒一份财产〔在〕私人宗教里是可能的，在国家里却办不到；而且，那些本来是虔诚举动的事情，如今也跟公开的荣誉绑在了一起。

en: a) It ought to seem a difficult task to set up a system of religious and moral truths that could have the free assent of all, or at least of most, since we regard it as a necessary requirement of a folk religion that it not force its doctrines on anyone, that it suffer constraint of no man's conscience — it ought to seem difficult, if one considers even superficially the infinite variety of the systems and hypotheses that have been devised by philosophers and theologians since reason has developed to ideas and to speculation about them.

Precisely this experience, that so many kinds of representation are possible and that, however bizarre some seem to us, they are yet tied to general ideas or needs of humanity [and] have always found their adherents, and at the same time the experience that, as soon as an importance is put into a certain way of representing things by public command or prohibition, not only the freedom of conscience of human beings is violated, but a dangerous fanaticism can easily be kindled — these experiences give precisely for the dogmas of a folk religion the rule that they should be as simple as possible, should contain nothing that the general human reason does not acknowledge — nothing whereby something would be determined, something dogmatically asserted that exceeds the bounds of reason, even if the authority for it should have its origin in heaven itself.
zh: a）要立起一套宗教和道德的真理体系，让它能得所有人、至少是大多数人自由的赞同，这看来该是件很难的事，因为我们认为，一种民间宗教必须做到不把自己的学说强加于人，不逼迫任何人的良心——只要稍微看一看那些体系和假设的无限纷繁，就会觉得这事确实难；这些体系和假设，是自从理性发展到观念、并开始对观念作思辨以来，由哲学家和神学家们想出来的。

正是这条经验——这么多种表象方式都行得通，而且不管有些在我们看来多么古怪，它们总还是挂在人类的某些普通观念或需要上，总还是找得到自己的拥护者——同时也是这条经验：只要凭公开的命令或禁止给某一种表象方式加上了分量，人的良心自由就不光受了侵犯，还很容易点起危险的热狂——这两条经验正好给民间宗教的教义定下一条规则：教义要尽可能简单，不要包含普通人类理性不承认的东西——不要包含任何规定什么、独断地断言什么、越出理性界限的东西，哪怕它的权限是从天上来的。

en: Such doctrines expose themselves to the danger, surely coming sooner or later, of being claimed and attacked by reason; the premature fruits can then perhaps be stifled, suppressed, struck off — but with advancing ripeness neither pyres for the writers or merely for their writings nor conjured symbols will halt the evil whose seed lies indestructible in human nature itself.

For irresistibly reason leads to the great principle of the self-sufficiency of duty and of virtue, which to want to promote through more roundabout or more heterogeneous motives than merely through the connection with the idea of God is already desecration; and if men of this faith do not hold the role of the miraculous doctrine to be altogether detrimental, harmful to morality, but favourable to despotism, they yet value their business only as being at most a leading-rein for the crude mob.

Now, convinced of the identity of their essence with their rational faith, each seeks in his own way to render his opponents powerless — one disputes positive religion with grounds taken from it or from its documents themselves, one with the weapons of wit, another is satisfied by his conviction that he actually [holds] the positive doctrines to be insignificant, yet because they are something hallowed in the faith of peoples, he seeks to accommodate them to his ideas.

We find it with so many men who developed the idea of morality purely out of their own heart and beheld in it, as in a mirror, its beauty and were enraptured by it, and whose soul was fullest of esteem for virtue and moral greatness — with a Spinoza, Shaftesbury, Rousseau, Kant —: the higher their esteem for morality and for the morality of Christ's doctrine rises, the more heterogeneous, the more dispensable the rest seems to them.
zh: 这类学说会给自己招来一种危险，这危险或早或晚总会可靠地到来：理性要来追究它、攻击它；那些早熟的果子到那时也许会被掐掉、压下去、打落——可是随着成熟继续推进，不论是给作者、或者只给他们的著作架起的火堆，还是被念过咒的象征，都挡不住这祸害，因为它的种子就不可毁灭地躺在人的本性里。
因为理性不可抗拒地通向那条大原则：义务和美德自身就足够了；想靠比单纯与神的观念相联结更绕弯、更杂异的动力去促进它们，就已经是一种亵渎；而信奉这套东西的人，即便不把那神奇学说的作用看成全然有害、对道德有损、却对专制有利，他们至少也把自己的行当看得不过是给粗野的群氓套上的一根笼头而已。
如今，每个人既然确信自己的本质跟自己的理性信仰是同一的，就各按自己的方式去让对手失去力量——有人用从实证宗教本身、或从它的文献里取来的理由去反驳它，有人用的是机智的武器，还有人只要自己心里确信：他其实认为那些实证学说是无关紧要的，可因为它们在各民族信仰里是神圣的东西，他便设法把它们迁就自己的观念。
我们在许多人身上都看得到这一点，他们纯粹从自己心里发展出道德的观念，并在这观念里像在镜子里一样看见它的美，为它心醉，他们的灵魂对美德和道德伟大满怀敬重——在斯宾诺莎、莎夫茨伯里、卢梭、康德身上——：他们对道德、对基督学说中的道德越敬重，其余的东西在他们看来就越杂异、越可以不要。

en: The mysteries, the incomprehensible dogmas [are] conceivable neither for reason or understanding — precisely because they are incomprehensible — nor any more for the imagination; for it they are wholly and entirely contradictory.27) When such doctrines are in question, all three must suspend their usual functions, they must put up with being entirely dispensed with for the time being, for their laws are here just as unusable as if I wanted to measure wine by the ell or fit a caricature into the form of a copy of Apollo's head.
So memory remains, which takes in certain combinations of words, to keep them for itself, to isolate them and to let the understanding see as little of them as possible.
zh: 这些奥秘、这些不可理解的教义，〔既〕不是理性或知性所能设想的——正因为它们不可理解——也同样不是想象力所能设想的；对想象力来说，它们完全是自相矛盾的。27）一谈到这类学说，这三者就都得停下自己平常的活计，得容忍人家把它们整个撇在一边，因为它们的法则在这里同样用不上，就像我想用尺子去量酒、或想把一幅漫画塞进阿波罗头像的样子里一样。
于是就只剩下记忆，它把某些词的组合收进来，替自己保住这些组合、把它们孤立起来，尽量不让知性看见。

en: Their main use is still left to us, namely insofar as these incomprehensible doctrines concern the heart, contain the practical demands that are made on the human being, the impulses they put into his hands, and the hopes of what they promise him.
Some of these doctrines are so constituted that in themselves they have no practical moment, but contain this only in association with others.
zh: 它们的主要用处还留给我们，就是说，只要这些不可理解的学说关系到心，包含着向人提出的实践要求、它们交到人手里的动力，以及它们向人承诺的事情所带来的希望。
这些学说里有一些是这样的：它们本身并没有实践的环节，只有跟别的学说合在一起才包含这一环节。

en: In general the first law of all these doctrines must be that they point out to the human being no [other] way of pleasing God than that through a good walk of life, or give no other motive for morally good action than [the] purely moral one.
Religion sets up the concept of pleasing God in a more or less pure sense.

From the sense of seeking to stand before God as the ideal of holiness, down to that of being exclusively and especially well off with him on account of some sensuous exercise, there are a host of shadings, which indeed can never be thought of as sufficiently separated from one another and purely.
zh: 总的说来，这全部学说的第一条法则必须是：它们给人指出的取悦神的方式，只能是靠良好的生活方式；或者，它们为道德上好的行为给出的动力，只能是纯粹道德的动力。
宗教把“取悦神”这个概念提出来时，意义有纯有杂。
从想作为神圣性的理想而在神面前站得住这个意思，一直降下来，到靠某种感性的练习就能独占地、特别地在他那里得好处，中间有一大堆层次，这些层次当然从来没能彼此分得足够清楚、想得足够纯粹。

en: However much, then, the concept of pleasing God, which religion sets up as the highest goal, is capable of impure propositions, it must all the more carefully prevent any practically harmful representation from creeping in with them.
zh: 所以，宗教把“取悦神”这一概念立为最高的目标，这概念再怎么能容纳不纯粹的命题，宗教就越要小心提防，不让任何在实践中害人的表象混进来。

en: In itself the demand is properly a contradiction, that doctrines exceeding our reason and imagination, as soon as they stand in any relation to the practical, should show us no other way than that of a good walk of life, no other way of pleasing God than this; for if they showed us no new way, they would not be incomprehensible doctrines, not mysteries.

Such doctrines, then, which demand of us only certain exercises — be it with the mouth or with hands and feet, be it a chime of feelings or be it certain abstinences and chastisements of the body, or certain things to believe — in order to please the holy being, so that one could thereby be released from the law of morality, dispensed from it — a web of such doctrines, let them be documented in the faith of peoples and of history with the holiest seals, reason must reject it; in its demand to be morally good it can let nothing be bargained away.
zh: 本来，这个要求自己就是个矛盾：那些超出我们理性和想象力的学说，一旦跟实践沾上任何关系，就该只给我们指出良好生活方式这一条路，只指出这一种取悦神的方式；因为，要是它们没给我们指出什么新路，那它们就不是不可理解的学说，也就不是奥秘了。
那么，这样一些学说，只要求我们做某些练习——或者用嘴，或者用手脚，或者是一串感受的钟声，或者是身体上的某些禁绝和责罚，或者是相信某些事情——为的是取悦那神圣的本质，好让人凭这个就可以不受道德法则的约束、从中得到豁免——这样一些学说织成的一张网，哪怕它在各民族的信仰和历史里用最神圣的印玺作过证，理性也必须把它扔掉；在它要求人道德上好的这件事上，理性一点也不能让人打折扣。

en: How abandoned the edifice of such states, or merely of classes of human beings, is, where these principles are in vogue, where all natural relations are twisted round by this unmoral-religious galimatias, the history of all times has taught, and the sad picture of the states where these systems still rule — e.g. in the Papal States, in Naples — still teaches it today, and only the never wholly destroyable goodness of human nature, which here is indeed mangled enough, only the necessity of civil laws, which, in order to make it possible for society to hold together at a pinch, must correct those principles somewhat, prevent the vices and evil inclinations from being wholly consistent with the doctrines by which they are nourished, unpunished and justified.
zh: 在这些原则盛行的地方，在一切自然关系都被这套不道德—宗教的胡言乱语扭歪的地方，这样的国家、或者哪怕只是这样一些人群的构造有多么糟糕，历代的历史已经教给我们了，今天那些还由这类体系统治着的国家——比如教会国、那不勒斯——的惨状也还在教给我们；只有人性里那永远毁不尽的善良（它在这里当然已经被糟蹋得够呛），只有市民法律的必要性（为了勉强让社会还能聚在一起，这些法律不得不在某些地方纠正那些原则），才拦住那些恶习和坏倾向，使它们不至于跟滋养它们、让它们不受惩罚还理直气壮的学说完全一致到底。

en: I count in here the publicly authorized faith that through hearing masses and the traffic in indulgences one can not only buy off one's sins but stand in nothing behind a good man — that bodily and other punishments are set upon difference in opinion — further, that criminals are withdrawn from the arm of justice by asylums and taken under the protection of the interpreters of the Godhead — that it is not only more meritorious as faith, but is publicly arranged, that only the beggar is favoured, while the industrious man fares badly.

And here there is talk not merely of the doctrines of some sophists or empiricists, who may with philosophical acuteness have found the principles that fix the difference between virtue and vice not well enough established, or [of] voluptuaries who in their life never bothered further about it or whose passions prevented them from hearing the voice of virtue — it is not of such individuals, as there are everywhere, that there is talk, but of this: that those principles, which invert morality and dishonour both humanity and the Godhead, are not merely treated by idle minds in studies or on lecture-chairs — as for instance, without noticeable harm to the commonwealth, happiness is adopted by a professor, otherwise empirical propositions by others, as the principle of morals or of natural right — not only [are they] publicly taught, but, what speaks more livingly than doctrines, are woven most intimately into the whole context of the state.

Men who feel the need of better principles, as also the otherwise good people in such states, cannot walk on the permitted highway of degradation and vice, [and] bring their better feeling into a connection with those principles through such turns, whose weakness they must hide from their understanding, but which yet satisfy their heart.
zh: 我把公开得到认可的信仰也算在这里：靠听弥撒和买卖赎罪券，人不但能把自己的罪买掉，还能在什么都不比好人差——身体上的和其他惩罚，是按意见上的分歧来定的——还有，罪犯靠避难所被从正义的手臂里抽走，受到神的解释者们的庇护——还有，不只是作为信仰更算功德，而且是由公家安排好的：只有乞丐得照顾，勤劳的人反倒过得糟。

而这里说的并不只是某些智者派或经验论者的学说，他们也许凭哲学上的锐利，觉得那些划定美德与恶习之别的原则还不够牢靠；或者〔说的是〕那些浪荡子，他们一辈子再没为此操过心，或者他们的情欲使他们听不见美德的声音——说的不是这样一些到处都有的个别人，而是这件事：那些颠倒道德、既侮辱人类又侮辱神的诸原则，并不只是由书房里、讲台上的闲脑袋在处理——就像一位教授把幸福、别的人把另外一些经验性的命题拿来当作道德或自然法的基础，而并不见对国家共同体有什么明显的害处那样——它们不只是被公开讲授，而且，还有比讲授更活的东西：它们已经最紧密地织进了国家的整个联系之中。
那些感到需要更好原则的人，还有这类国家里本来善良的人，既然走不了那条被允许的堕落与恶习的大道，就用这样一些拐弯的说法，把自己较好的感受跟那些原则连起来；这些说法的软弱，他们必须在自己的知性面前藏起来，可它们毕竟让他们的心得到满足。

en: Such doctrines must therefore be absolutely rejected by reason, whether it chooses principles for the individual or more general ones that concern the economy of a whole state.
zh: 所以，理性无论是为自己挑选个人的原则，还是挑选涉及整个国家经济的更普遍的原则，这类学说都必定要被它断然抛弃。

en: But otherwise the positive doctrines of a religion, those that the development of human reason could not itself discover, indicate a better purpose, and especially in more recent times people have always been very eagerly concerned to cultivate and to seek out the practical moment in every dogmatic doctrine.
zh: 不过在别的方面，一种宗教的实证学说——也就是人类理性自身的发展无法找到的那些学说——指出的是更好的目的；尤其在近代，人们总是非常热心地努力去培养和寻找每一种教义学说里的实践环节。

en: People have come back from the efforts to make the mysteries of religion acceptable through reason, and now they set great store by the distinction that those doctrines are indeed above reason but not against reason, a distinction that does indicate a certain shy regard for reason, a certain reverence for its knightly office, but in the end does not amount to much; for if reason is the highest judge of its faith, then it will not accept, will not believe, that which it believes it cannot attain in the whole range of its use and its application of power28), - just as, when after all attempts at navigation no north-west passage through America is discovered, geography boldly asserts that there is none.
zh: 人们已经从那种努力里退了回来——不再设法通过理性把宗教的奥秘说得可以接受——现在却非常看重这样一个区别：那些学说是超乎理性之上的，但并不违背理性。这个区别固然表示对理性有一种畏怯的顾及，对它那种骑士般的职分有一种敬畏，但归根到底没有什么了不起；因为理性既然是它自己信仰的最高裁判者，那么凡是它认为自己用尽全部运用和力量也达不到的东西28），它就不会接受，不会相信——这就好比，航海的一切尝试都没有发现一条穿过美洲的西北航道，地理学于是就大胆断言：没有这样一条航道。

en: Such words, then, which are lost to reason, for it cannot comprehend them, which are unthinkable for the understanding, unrepresentable for the imagination, and usable only for memory, can still have an importance for man only for the heart, only with regard to their influence on the determination of the will.
zh: 所以，这类话语对理性来说是白丢了——因为理性没法以概念把握它们；它们对知性来说不可思考，对想象力来说不可设想，只还能供记忆使用；它们对人还有的那点重要性，就只在于对心说话，只在于它们对意志规定的影响。

en: Undeniably, many a side of the superhuman Christian religious doctrines has as its purpose and consequence not genuine morality but only legality.

If they are capable of a refinement and a turn in order to become moral, it must yet be admitted - previously the thing was not taken so exactly - that these attempts were first occasioned by the objections and reproaches of opponents, and for a long, long time they were in fact used only to
zh: 不可否认，基督教那些超乎人的宗教学说中，有不少方面无论就目的还是就结果来说，都不是真正的道德，而只是合法性。
即使它们能够经过一番提炼和转向而变成道德的，也必须承认——从前对这事情并没有看得这么仔细——这些尝试最初是由对手的反驳和责备引起的，而且在很长很长的时间里，它们实际上只是被用来

en: to storm the dreamer's imagination, where the torch of the law burns dim29)
zh: 去攻占做梦者的想象，那里法则的火把昏暗地燃着29）

en: (or have occasioned the hope of expecting morality in a supernatural way - or produced the fear of being made worse in just this way).

I need only appeal to the representations, on the one hand, of the rewards that were placed in mystical blisses, in childish, trifling, or on an immoral pride resting distinctions, and on the other hand, of the punishments, which are painted even more eloquently than the rewards through their garish, sensuous images of the torments of hell, where the devil with ever-new inventive power torments the soul eternally without hope of rescue, eternally, eternally -: many an imagination, as is not to be wondered at, which has succumbed under the power of these representations, has been shattered, have brought many people to despair, to frenzy.
zh: （或者引起了这样的希望：以超自然的方式期待道德——或者产生了这样的恐惧：恰恰会以这种方式变得更坏。）
我只需举出这样一些表象：一方面是奖赏——它们被放在神秘的至福里，放在幼稚的、儿戏般的、或者建立在一种不道德的骄傲之上的优越之处；另一方面是惩罚——它们比奖赏描画得还要雄辩，用的是那些刺眼的、感性的地狱酷刑图景：在那里，魔鬼以层出不穷的发明不断折磨着灵魂，永远没有得救的希望，永远、永远——：不少想象力，这并不奇怪，就在这些表象的力量下垮掉了、被弄坏了，把许多人拖进了绝望、拖进了疯狂。

en: If the imagination of Greek Bacchantes ran over into the delusion of seeing the Godhead itself present, and into the wildest outbursts of an unruly drunkenness, then this was an enthusiasm of joy, of jubilation, - an enthusiasm that soon returned again to ordinary life.

But those religious excesses of the imagination are outbursts of the saddest, most anxious despair, which ruins the organs from the ground up, and often incurably; the data, even the more definite features for these pictures are given by dogmatics, not merely the doctrine, and it is left only to the more or less lively imagination of the teacher to present them more garishly or less terribly.
zh: 希腊酒神女祭司的想象力即使失控到发狂，以为亲眼看见神本身就在场，失控到无法无天的醉态中最狂野的发作，那也是一种欢乐的、欢呼的热情——一种很快就会回到平常生活中去的热情。
但想象力在宗教上的那些放纵，是最悲哀、最惶恐的绝望的发作，它把人的机体从根子上搞坏，而且常常无法医治；这些图景的材料，甚至其中比较确定的笔触，都是由教义学给出的，不只是那条学说本身；至于把它们画得更刺眼还是不那么可怕，就只取决于教师的想象力有多活跃了。

en: The expectation(s) of rewards and punishments in another world are so naturally grounded in the practical need of reason to establish a connection between this and another life, that this doctrine has been a main point of all religions; but in order to be worthy of a moral religion, caution must be applied in its treatment - in order to fix it in the faith of peoples.
zh: 对另一个世界里的奖赏和惩罚的期待，如此自然地扎根在理性的实践需要里——就是要在这一世和另一世之间建立起一种联系——所以这条学说一直是所有宗教的一个要点；但要配得上一种道德的宗教，处理它时就必须谨慎——为的是把它固定在民众的信仰里。

en: What cultivation of the power of imagination is involved here does not yet come into consideration; only the doctrine, insofar as it rests on the super-rational principles that the Christian religion gives us, - although faith in the images of the imagination as in dogmas is also demanded.

The doctrine of the resurrection of the bodies is of no great moral importance; only it has presumably had the in itself insignificant consequence that through it the concept of the human soul, as a spiritual incorporeal being, could not become more general; or rather, the hope of a continuance of personal existence - against which death, the extinction of that existence, speaks so naturally - since it did not have the idea of an incorporeal, imperishable, immortal being, helped itself along with it by letting the body revive as its self, not merely as its familiar companion.
zh: 这里还不考虑其中有多少是想象力的培养，只考虑那条学说本身，就它建立在基督教给我们的那些超理性的原则之上而言——尽管人们也要求把想象力的图像当作教义来信。
肉体复活的学说在道德上并不重要；它大概只有过一个本身无关紧要的后果，就是由于它，关于人的灵魂是一个精神的、无形体的存在者这个概念没能变得更普遍；或者不如说，对人格性存在延续下去的盼望——而死亡、这种存在的熄灭又那么自然地与它作对——既然它没有无形体的、不会朽坏的、不死的存在者这个观念，就只好拿身体来帮忙，让身体作为它自己、而不只是作为它熟悉的同伴再活过来。

en: The hope of a compensation for sufferings endured is a comforting thought, a thought that we demand of justice, but in this we must nevertheless accustom ourselves not to regard everything that happens contrary to our expectation as an injustice; we must accustom ourselves more to regard ourselves as more dependent on nature.

The entanglement of our political and civil relations and the inequality in the manner of life and in the goods of fortune has increased not only misery of every kind but also the irritability and the susceptibility to it; to the pains to which we are exposed by virtue of our nature and of our manner of life that so often deviates from it, there very often joins itself also impatience, an impatience that springs from the demand that everything should go well with us and according to our wish, and from the belief that we suffer injustice in misfortune.
zh: 对所受痛苦得到补偿的希望是一个安慰人的想法，一个我们向正义要求来的想法；但在这件事上我们总得习惯：不要把凡是与我们的期待相反发生的事情都看成不公正；我们更要习惯把自己看得更依赖自然。
我们的政治关系和市民关系的纠葛，以及生活方式和财富上的不平等，不仅增加了各式各样的苦难，也增加了对苦难的敏感和易受感染的脾气；除了我们凭本性、凭那种常常与本性强背离的生活方式而遭受的痛苦之外，还常常加上一种不耐烦——它来自这样一种要求：一切都该顺顺当当、称心如意；也来自这样一种信念：遭遇不幸是受了不公正的对待。

en: Behind the pretended contempt for the goods and honours of this world there very often lurks an envy, very ill-contrasted, of those who possess them; the contempt is very often rather an annoyance at it, and the lack of them is then regarded as an injustice, as a suffering, for which we should likewise deserve compensation.

Many people, in the conviction that the sufferings of this world are not worth the glory of the future one, believe that without suffering they can have no part in it at all; in a quiet enjoyment of this life combined with the fulfilment of their duties, they still live full of vigilance over their virtue, indeed actually full of anxiety - and create for themselves a mass of either real or dreamed-up sufferings and complain30) about this world as about a vale of tears, where yet they really have nothing to complain about.
All dispositions of this kind lead away from the spirit, from the truth, of a moral connection between this life and the future one that is to be hoped for.
zh: 在对这世上的财富和荣誉所装作的那副蔑视背后，常常藏着对拥有它们的人的嫉妒，而且对照得很难看；这种蔑视往往倒更像是一种恼怒；而缺少这些东西，于是就被看成一种不公正、一种痛苦，认为我们也该为此得到补偿。
许多人确信，这世上的痛苦配不上将来那世上的荣耀，于是认为没有痛苦，他们根本就不能分享那份荣耀；他们一面安静地享受这辈子，一面尽自己的义务，却仍然活得满是对自己美德的警觉，其实简直是活在恐惧里——还给自己造出一大堆或者现实的、或者空想的痛苦，抱怨30）这个世界是个苦难之谷，可他们其实真没有什么可抱怨的。
所有这类心绪，都使人离开这样一种精神、这样一种真理：这辈子和将来那辈子之间有一种值得盼望的道德联系。

en: A distinguishing doctrine of Christianity, unknown to reason, is the frightful alternative, where there is no middle term, that the fate awaiting human beings in another world is either eternal bliss or eternal damnation, - an alternative which, if human beings' representations of the future after this life were as certain, as reliable, as the certainty that quinine bark cures fever, - which, I say, would leave man in this life, after which the kingdom of grace comes to an end and the kingdom of inexorable justice begins, not a moment's rest, but would place him in a state of the most tormenting uncertainty, which in the feeling of its imperfection wavered eternally between the fear of the judge of the world and the hope from the gracious, forgiving father, - a tormenting state, which is only less frequent because man's nature is inconsistent with regard to those of its principles that are not grounded in itself but only driven into the head from outside.
zh: 基督教有一条区别性的、理性所不知道的学说，就是那个可怕的二择一，中间没有第三条路：人在另一个世界等待着的命运，要么是永恒的至福，要么是永恒的永罚——这个二择一，假如人们对死后将来的表象像「金鸡纳树皮能治疟疾」那样确实、那样可靠，那么我说，它就会让活在这辈子的人一刻也不得安宁，因为这辈子一结束，恩典的国就终止，毫不容情的正义的国就开始；它就会把人抛进一种最折磨人的不确定状态，这种状态在自身不完善的感觉中，永远在「畏惧世界审判者」和「盼望仁慈赦免的父亲」之间摇摆——这是一种痛苦的状态，它之所以不那么常见，只是因为人的本性对它自己的某些原则并不一贯，这些原则不是扎根在人自己心里，而只是从外面被塞进脑袋里的。

en: But of very great practical importance is the story of Jesus, not merely his teachings or those ascribed to him.

To love the good, to practise right rightly, not to owe the semblance of virtue to mere momentary good impulses but to love it from free choice, for that principles are needed, a preponderance of our metaphysics over our physics, of abstract ideas over the sensuous.
When will it come to this with the human race, that principles rule more than feelings, laws more than individuals?

If virtue, said Plato, appeared visibly among men, then all mortals would have to love it - Plato surely did believe in virtuous men, but in order to inspire men to zealous admiration he demanded virtue itself.

The story of Jesus presents to us not merely a man who had first formed himself in solitude and then devoted his time solely to the improvement of men, who finally sacrificed even his life to this purpose.

To cite the best-known example, Socrates could in that respect just as well have been held up to us as a mirror, as a model; he drew his wisdom in the tumult of active life, in the battles where he saved his friend at the risk of his life, he devoted his life to the improvement of his fellow citizens, and in the end truth handed him the cup of poison, which he emptied with the most sublime calm.
What is lacking to us here for a model of virtue?
Was not Socrates a man with no more powers than we have, can we not set about the work of imitation with the hope of being able to attain the degree of perfection in our way of life just as well?
What did it cost Christ to give the help he gave to the sick? - a word.

Furnished with divine power, to which neither sensuousness could oppose any faint inclination or feeling, nor could lack of means and strength stand in the way, should the blameless life of Jesus, his steadfastness, his calm in suffering, not appear to us as worthy of admiration and not entice us to imitation, we who are wholly stripped bare, without hope of bringing it so far.

But the imagination pays no heed to this reasoning of cold understanding, and it is precisely the admixture, the addition of the divine that qualifies the virtuous man Jesus as an ideal of virtue, - without the divine in his person we would have only the man, but here a true superhuman ideal, which is nevertheless not foreign to the human soul, insofar as it must think itself removed from it.

Besides, this ideal has the further advantage of not being a cold abstraction; its individualisation, that we hear it speak, see it act, brings it, which is already akin to our spirit, still closer for our feeling.

Here, then, there has appeared to the believer no longer a virtuous man but virtue itself: in the former case we are always inclined to presuppose still secret shadows, or at least a former struggle, as with Socrates only from the physiognomy, - here faith has the spotless, yet not disembodied, virtue.
zh: 但有极大实践上的重要性的，是耶稣的故事，而不只是他的、或者人们归到他名下的那些学说。
要爱善，要正当地行使权利，不是单靠一时良好的冲动而显得有美德，而是出于自由的选择去爱美德，这就需要原则，需要我们的形而上学压过我们的物理本性，抽象的观念压过感性的东西。
人类要到什么时候才能走到这一步：原则比感受更占支配地位，法则比个人更占支配地位？
柏拉图说过，如果美德在人间可见地显现出来，那么所有有死的人就都不得不爱它——柏拉图大概还是相信有有美德的人的，但为了激起人们热心的赞叹，他要求的是美德本身。
耶稣的故事摆在我们面前的，不只是一个先独自在孤寂中把自己培养出来、后来又把全部时间用在改善人身上、最终为这个目的连自己的命也牺牲掉的人。
举最著名的例子来说，在这方面，苏格拉底本来同样可以被立为我们的一面镜子、一个榜样；他的智慧是在忙碌生活的纷扰中、在战场上汲取来的——他在那里冒着生命危险救了自己的朋友；他把一生献给了改善自己的同胞；最后是真理递给他那杯毒药，他以最崇高的平静把它喝干。
这里还缺什么，才够得上一个美德的榜样呢？
苏格拉底不也是一个力量并不比我们多的人吗？我们难道不能怀着这样的希望去做仿效这件事：在我们的生活方式中也同样达到那个完善的程度？
基督给病人帮助，花的是什么代价？——一句话。
耶稣既然有神的力量，感性既不能对它提出任何轻微的偏好或感受，手段和力量的缺乏也挡不住它，那么耶稣那无可指摘的一生、他的坚定、他在痛苦中的平静，难道不应当让我们觉得可佩、不应当诱使我们去仿效吗——而我们却是完全赤手空拳、没有希望能做到那个地步的。
但想象力不管冷静知性的这套推理；恰恰是神性的掺入、神性的附加，才把那个有美德的凡人耶稣提升为美德的理想——没有他身上的神性，我们得到的就只是一个人；而在这里却是一个真正超乎人的理想，它对于人的灵魂来说并不陌生，尽管灵魂不得不认为自己离它很远。
此外，这个理想还有一个好处：它不是冷冰冰的抽象物；它被个体化——我们听见它说话，看见它行动——这就把它，这个本来已经和我们的精神相近的东西，对我们的感受来说拉得更近。
所以在这里，向信徒显现的已经不再是一个有美德的人，而是美德本身：面对前者，我们总倾向于假定还有暗中的阴影，或者至少有过一番搏斗——在苏格拉底那里，这只能从面相上看出来；而在这里，信仰拥有的是毫无瑕疵、却并非脱去形体的美德。

en: The addition of the divine in Jesus, instead of apparently weakening our zeal in imitating, since by the consideration of the impossibility of approaching him it should deter us, is perhaps more favourable to our inclination towards ideals that are more than human.
zh: 耶稣身上那附加的神性，表面上并没有削弱我们效法的热忱——因为一想到根本不可能接近他，这反倒该叫我们退缩——它也许倒是更迎合我们那种向往超人之理想的倾向。

en: But just as, in order to be a good imitator, one must oneself be a piece of an original - as in everything else, so even more in the moral sphere, otherwise it is only something forced, something in which one can see that it is not natural, where here and there something is not quite in its place, will not quite fit, stands out from the rest -, so virtue must especially be something one has oneself experienced, something one has oneself practised.

The virtue that is copied after others, learned by rote, has something awkward about it, something that cannot stand up against experience and an advancing acquaintance with the world, that has no value, no merit.

Thus the crowd, countless people of no consequence, i.e. without noble feelings, without delicate situations, without situations where virtue and strength or patience could show themselves, who nevertheless, without being remotely in similar situations or a similar activity, wanted absolutely to be equal to their archetype, have attached the name of high virtues to their little trifles.

Hence the crowd of complaining sufferers, who lacked nothing, - of the persecuted, whom one left in peace or who themselves had no rest until one persecuted them, - the crowd of teachers, whose wisdom no human being needed.

The model of virtue that human beings formed for themselves after their ideal naturally also took on the tone of those virtues that stand out chiefly in the ideal, but what was imitated then brought it about that these virtues frequently degenerated, were clumsily applied.
From the wish to instruct, self-righteousness has arisen, and from that, intolerance.
zh: 但正如一个人要想成为好的效法者，自己本身就必须有一部分是原创的——在别的事情上如此，在道德上就更是如此，否则它就只是勉强做出来的东西，是让人一眼就看出不自然的东西，这里那里总有点不在自己的位置上，总有点合不来，跟其余的部分格格不入——所以美德尤其必须是自己亲身经历过的、自己亲身实践过的东西。
那种照着别人模仿来的、死记硬背下来的美德，带着一种笨拙，一种经不起经验、经不起对世界日益增长的认识的东西，既没有价值，也没有功劳。
于是民众，无数无关紧要的人，也就是说，没有高尚的情感、没有微妙的处境、没有能让美德和力量或耐心显露出来的场合，却又根本不曾处在类似的处境或类似的活动中，却硬要跟自己的原型一模一样，就把自己那些鸡毛蒜皮冠上了崇高美德的名号。
由此就有了那一群抱怨的受苦者，他们其实什么也不缺，——那一群被迫害者，人们本来让他们安安静静待着，或者他们自己一直不得安宁，直到有人来迫害他们，——那一群教师，他们的智慧根本没有人需要。
人们按自己的理想给自己塑造出来的美德典范，自然也就带上了那些在理想中最突出的美德所特有的调子，但学来的东西随后就造成这些美德常常变味、被笨拙地用在不对的地方。
从想要教导别人这件事里，生出了自以为有理，又从这生出不宽容。

en: [The] doctrine of providence, a concept peculiar to the Christian religion, [is] a concept of reason, which we really should not make use of in any single case, since it is not a concept of the understanding and therefore explains nothing.
zh: [关于]护佑的学说，一个基督教特有的概念，[是]一个理性的概念，我们其实不该在任何个别场合使用它，因为它不是一个知性概念，因而什么也解释不了。

en: Very many opponents of what is peculiar to Christianity have on the other hand shown the greatest respect for the moral teaching of the Christian religion, - however much they have made the doctrine of the Trinity, of reconciliation, of original sin the object of their mockery or of their other weapons, so much have they been inspired by the moral teaching of Christianity and have exalted it as a benefit that has befallen the human race.

And in fact, the purest system of moral teaching, which absolutely excludes all material principles, has nowhere been able to attach itself to the Christian religion more freely than in regard to moral teaching.

And however much, again, others have found individual pronouncements of Jesus or of his apostles, individual commands or expressions of sentiments, incompatible with a pure moral teaching, it is just as certain that the whole spirit of the moral teaching of Christ can be brought into agreement with every most exalted moral teaching, that the most unconditional obedience to the law is inculcated in it.
zh: 许多反对基督教独有之处的人，反过来却对基督教的道德学说表现出最大的敬意，——不管他们怎样把三位一体说、和解说、原罪说当作嘲笑的对象或他们别的武器，他们照样被基督教的道德学说说得热血沸腾，把它当作降临到人类头上的一桩恩惠来推崇。
而且事实上，那套最纯粹的道德学说，那套绝对排斥一切实质性原则的学说，在任何地方都没有能像在道德学说方面这样毫不勉强地同基督教结合起来。
同样，另一些人固然发现耶稣或他使徒的个别说法、个别命令或心态的表白，与一种纯粹的道德学说不能相容，但同样确定的是，基督的道德学说的整个精神可以同任何一种最高尚的道德学说取得一致，其中所反复强调的，是对法则的无条件服从。

en: But the main thing is not whether the pronouncements of a pure moral teaching can be discovered in the teaching of Jesus; they can just as well be found in the writings of a Plato, a Xenophon, a Rousseau.

Nor is it to be counted against it that the practical principles are not brought into a system, or that at least all duties and the motives of the same are not definitely given; the main thing is in what light, in what connection, in what rank they are set up.
zh: 但主要的问题并不是，在耶稣的教导里能不能找到一种纯粹道德学说的说法；这些东西在柏拉图、色诺芬、卢梭的著作里同样找得到。
也不该计较这些实践原则没有被做成一个体系，或者至少没有把一切义务以及义务的动机都明确地给出来；主要的问题在于，它们是放在什么光亮之下、什么联系之中、什么等级次序上被提出来的。

en: John's address to the people was: Repent; [that] of Christ: Repent and believe the gospel; [that] of the apostles: Believe in Christ, - and the way of the latter has maintained itself down to the present day in all schools, compendiums, sermons.

Even today, when the spirit, the ideas of the age, no longer have the need of an atonement for crimes, one begins, partly in order of time, partly in order of importance, by teaching us to know Christ as the reconciler of sins, who [has] fallen to the offended holiness of God as a sacrifice for mankind, of which every individual would need an atonement not in individual cases, but already for his existence and for his whole life.

Gratitude towards the person who has suffered and died for us - as if many millions had not already sacrificed themselves for lesser ends, with a smile, without bloody sweat of anguish, with joyfulness surrendered themselves for their king, for their fatherland, for their beloved - how much more readily would they have died for the human race! -, gratitude towards this death, the most important thing, the centre of our religion, the most solemn thing for the occupation of our imagination, is supposed to lead to the veneration of Christ and of God; to this veneration there belongs, among other things, the spread of his name etc., also finally piety, charity etc.
zh: 约翰对民众说的话是：悔改；基督的是：悔改并且相信福音；使徒的是：相信基督，——而后面这一条路，直到今天还保留在一切学校、教科书、布道里。
就是今天，在精神、时代的观念已经不再需要为罪行赎罪的时候，人们还是开头就讲——按时间说也好，按重要性说也好都如此——教我们认识基督是罪的赎罪者，他为人类作了献祭，献给了被冒犯的神的圣洁，而每一个个体不只是在个别场合，而是为自己的存在、为自己的整整一生，本来就需要这样的赎罪。

对那个为我们受了苦、为我们死了的人的感恩——好像还没有千百万的人为更小的目的牺牲过自己似的，他们带着微笑，没有血淋淋的恐惧汗水，满心欢喜地为自己的国王、为自己的祖国、为自己的爱人献出生命——他们要是为人类去死，那还不知会多么痛快！——对这种死亡的感恩，我们宗教中最重要的事、中心，供我们想象力去忙碌的最庄严的事，据说应当引向对基督和对神的敬拜；而属于这种敬拜的，除了别的，还有传扬他的名等等，最后还有虔诚、慈善等等。

en: By these detours we have arrived at moral teaching, but not in an ascending, rather in a descending line.

The reproach would therefore be unjust that the Christian religion does not promote morality at all; but how much those detours have harmed morality, by the fact that one so readily accepted them as the sole main ends, lies in broad daylight.
Even by this the goal of morality has been shifted out of sight, that one made not it, but bliss, the last end of these teachings.
zh: 经过这些绕路，我们才走到道德学说，但不是沿着上升的路线，而是沿着下降的路线。
所以，说基督教根本不促进道德，这个指责是不公正的；但这些绕路因为人们那么轻易就把它们当成了唯一的主要目的，究竟给道德造成了多大损害，是明摆着的。
人们把这些学说的最后目的不是定为道德，而是定为至福，单凭这一点，道德的目标就已经被挪出了视线。

en: The commendation of faith has frequently had the consequence that one contented oneself with a dead faith - of memory, of the mouth -, with feelings, and [oneself] spared the good sentiment and good actions.
Already the procedure of the apostles in receiving people into their congregation was entirely different from that which Christ observed with those whom he accepted as his friends.

For the former it sufficed if a crowd of mostly ignorant people had [themselves] so been set into astonishment by the eloquence of one or several hours that they believed their words and had themselves baptized by the apostles, and with that they were then made Christians.
This manner of conversion has been continued for many centuries and is still practised today on the whole in the same way on the Ganges, on the Orinoco, on the St. Lawrence.
zh: 对信仰的推崇经常带来的后果是，人们满足于一种死的信仰——记忆的、嘴巴的信仰——满足于感受，而[自己]省掉了好的心态和好的行动。
使徒们接纳人加入自己团体的做法，跟基督对待他所接纳为朋友的那些人的做法，已经完全不同。
对使徒们来说，只要一群多半无知的人[自己]被一个或几个钟头的雄辩弄得那么吃惊，以致相信了他们的话，让使徒给自己施了洗，这就够了，这样他们就成了现成的基督徒。
这种使人皈依的方式延续了许多个世纪，直到今天在恒河、在奥里诺科河、在圣劳伦斯河一带，大体上还是用同样的办法在做。

en: Because the grateful veneration of Christ, the spread of his name over the earth, is put forward as a main end, as a main duty, this has had the consequence that the reproach which Sittah makes in Nathan31) is not at all unjust.
For why send out missionaries, as long as there are still morally bad people among the Christians?

Not only the Catholics, the Protestants just as much and the English Church have extensive costly institutions, whose execution has cost much labour, sweat, hardships, even blood - in order with a name, with a history to fill the imagination of peoples who, according to their need, had already created their gods, their religion for themselves.
zh: 因为对基督的感恩敬拜、把他的名传遍大地，被说成是一个主要目的、一项主要义务，这就带来了这样的后果：西塔在《智者纳坦》³¹⁾里提出的指责，根本不是不公正的。
因为，只要基督徒当中还有道德败坏的人，派出传教士干什么呢？
不只是天主教徒，新教徒同样如此，英国教会也有规模庞大、花费昂贵的机构，执行这些机构耗费了大量的劳动、汗水、艰辛，甚至鲜血——只为了用一个名字、一段历史去填满那些民族的想象力，而那些民族早已按照自己的需要给自己造出了自己的神、自己的宗教。

en: When one writes about the Christian religion, one is at all times exposed to the danger of being accused of the error of forming an incorrect representation of its purpose and essence; and for whatever one finds to object to in the representation one forms of it, one is at once ready with the counter-answer that this does not touch the Christian religion, but only a certain representation of it.
If one begs that the doctrinal concept be shown to one, in which one may reliably come upon the pure system of the Christian religion, then the gentlemen will all answer with one mouth: is
zh: 只要一写到基督教，人就随时有被指责的危险，说他错在对其目的和本质抱有一种不正确的表象；而一旦他对人们为自己形成的那个表象挑出什么毛病，对方立刻就有话回过来：这触及的不是基督教，而只是基督教的某一种表象。
如果你请求他们，把那个教理概念拿给你看，说在其中可以靠得住地碰到基督教纯正的体系，那么各位先生就会异口同声地回答：是

en: Is my compendium not known to you, then? — But, gentlemen, your self-written compendiums, or those which you lay down as the basis of your system of faith, are themselves so
zh: 难道我的纲要您不知道吗？——可是先生们，你们自己写的那些纲要，或者你们拿来当作自己信仰体系之根据的那些，本身就是这样

en: different, that one must request you to agree among yourselves beforehand, before you give out something as not belonging to the Christian religion. — What in the following will be regarded as belonging to the Christian religion is either drawn directly from the New Testament, or — apart from very few textbooks and the convictions of individual enlightened men — is, one may well say, still the folk doctrine publicly acknowledged by the consistories and church councils, still the course taken in most pulpits and schools — at least the system in which the whole generation that has now grown up has presumably been brought up and instructed —, and it is therefore, one may well say, still important to throw light on much in this order of salvation, until sounder representations have more generally gained ground and those systems hold interest only, as it were, for the curious investigator in the spirit of times gone by.
I therefore believe I have not fallen into the error of those who give others the itch so that they may scratch.

No assurance would give me more pleasure than the one that, with regard to certain ways of representing things that seemed offensive to me, it had for that reason been unnecessary to remark on anything, because they had long been forgotten — if only I could take this assurance to be universally true.
zh: ……如此不同，以致人们不得不请求你们先彼此商量好，再来宣布什么东西不属于基督教。——下面被看作属于基督教的那些东西，要么是直接取自《新约》，要么就是——除去极少数教科书和个别开明人士的信念不算——大概仍然是各教会监理会和教会评议会公开承认的民众学说，仍然是大多数讲道台和学校里走的那条路——至少是那一套大概把如今已经长大的一整代人都教育、教导于其中的体系——；所以大概仍然值得在这套救恩次序里把有些东西照一照，直到更健全的表象更普遍地占了上风，而那些体系只还对好奇的研究者、在逝去时代的精神里有点意思。
所以我以为，我没有犯那种人的错误：先把疥疮过给别人，好让人去抓痒。
再没有哪种保证能比这一种更让我高兴：对于某些在我看来很刺眼的表象方式，本来就不必再提什么，因为它们早就被忘掉了——只要我能把这一保证当作普遍真实的东西接受下来。

en: The effect of religion is the strengthening of the motives of morality through the idea of God as moral lawgiver — and the satisfaction of the tasks of our practical reason with regard to the final end it has set for us, the highest good.

On account of these effects, religion can become the purpose of the legislators and the administrators of a state, and the natural need of human beings for it can be satisfied by them through special arrangements.

Usually the will of the nation has long since declared itself for a particular religion before the governments were able to set that religion as their purpose; only the propagation, the maintenance, the perpetual refreshing of the knowledge of it can a government make its purpose.

If one now knows how great the influence of the public arrangements for the preservation of a certain religious system is upon the mass of the nations in monarchical states, where the people is seldom in a condition to investigate for itself, to choose for itself, but behaves altogether passively in instruction, then it is surely permissible to ask: Is the religion that was once expedient for the people — otherwise it would not have turned to it — is this religion, in the same shape, under wholly changed circumstances, still just as expedient?

Was religion in its first origin so constituted that it was capable, with every change of the form of government, of enlightenment, both as general religion and as private religion, of keeping its dignity, its expediency, and of exercising its efficacy equally?

Has the spirit of the peoples itself gradually laid aside or changed whatever in it was perhaps temporal, or have those in power got it into their hands to dispense religion, and have these taken an interest in holding fast to the shape they inherited from their forefathers and in handing it on unchanged, as a precious good entrusted to them, into the hands of their successors?

Until changes became the need of a whole nation and could then no longer be held back, it has always required centuries; and the people was usually content with one blow, then soon let the handle be twisted out of its hands again, whereby further progress and several improvements were usually made impossible for centuries, even by the attachment to the new find and the mistrust that one was out to tear it from their hands again.
zh: 宗教的作用在于，借神作为道德立法者这一观念来加强德性的动力——并且就实践理性给我们设定的终极目的、即至善而言，满足我们实践理性的任务。
由于这些作用，宗教可以成为国家的立法者和管理者所要达到的目的，而人对宗教的自然需要，也可以由他们通过特别的设施来满足。
通常，民族的意志早已为某一种特定的宗教表明了态度，然后政府才可能把这种宗教立为目的；政府能立为目的的，只有把它传播下去、维持下去，以及不断地把对它的认识重新翻新。
既然人们知道，在君主制国家里，为了维持某一套宗教体系而设的公共设施，对各国民众的影响有多大——在那里，人民很少处在能够自己去考察、自己去选择的状态，在受教这件事上干脆是消极被动的——，那么大概可以问一句：那种曾经对人民合用的宗教——否则人民也不会转向它——，在完全改变了的境况下、以同一个形态，是不是还同样合用？
宗教在它最初的起源处是不是这样构成的：无论政体、启蒙怎样变化，它作为普遍宗教也好、作为私人宗教也好，都能保住自己的尊严和合用，并且同样发挥它的效力？
是各民族的精神自己把其中也许是暂时性的东西逐渐放下或改掉了，还是掌权者把分发宗教这件事抓到了自己手里，并且对这样一件事发生了兴趣：把自己从祖先那里继承来的形态牢牢抓住，当作一份托付给自己的珍贵财产，原封不动地再交到后继者手里？
直到种种改变成为整个民族的需要、再也拦不住，这总要花上几百年；而人民通常挨一下就满足了，随后又很快让人把权柄从自己手里拧走，于是进一步的进展、若干改善，往往几百年都不可能——甚至是因为对新到手的东西的那份依恋，以及那种猜疑：人家就是要把它再从他们手里夺走。

en: A religion can be considered
zh: 一种宗教可以被考察

en: a) with regard to its doctrines
zh: a）就它的教理而言

en: b) its traditions
zh: b）它的传统

en: c) its ceremonies
zh: c）它的仪式

en: d) its relation to the state, or as public religion — arrangements.
zh: d）它与国家的关系，或者作为公共宗教——设施。

en: What are the requirements of a folk religion with regard to these points of view — do we find them in the Christian religion?
zh: 就这些着眼点来说，一种民间宗教要具备哪些条件——我们在基督教里碰得到这些条件吗？

en: α) Practical reason sets before man, as the highest purpose of all his striving, it lays upon him the task: production of the highest good in the world, morality and the happiness appropriate to it.
zh: α）实践理性给人设定了他一切努力的最高目的，给他立下这个任务：在世界上造成至善，即道德和与它相称的幸福。

en: I believe I may take it as a fairly general doctrine of Christianity that the hope of an eternal bliss is what has the greatest interest for the Christian, in comparison with which everything else has only a subordinate value.
God's good pleasure in him is important to him because this God is the dispenser of that bliss.
This idea of bliss agrees, as regards its matter, fairly well with what reason posits.
The highest condition of the possibility of the highest good is, according to reason, the adequacy of the sentiment to the moral law.

According to the Christian religion, the highest condition of eternal bliss is faith in Christ and in the power of his reconciling death, and indeed not because this faith can in the end lead to morality, which would then after all be the proper condition and that faith only the means, but faith is itself the ground of God's good pleasure, and this good pleasure therefore gives eternal bliss to those who believe in Christ, which they could actually never have deserved.
zh: 我想我可以把这一点当作基督教相当普遍的教理：对永恒至福的希望，对基督徒来说是最要紧的事，跟它相比，别的都只有次要的价值。
神对他的悦纳之所以对他要紧，是因为这位神是那份至福的施予者。
这个至福的观念，就质料而言，跟理性所设定的东西相当一致。
按照理性，至善之所以可能，最高的条件是信念与道德法则相称。
按照基督教，永恒至福的最高条件是对基督、以及对他那和解之死的效力的信仰；而且并不是因为这种信仰最终能引向道德——那样一来道德才是真正的条件，而那种信仰只是手段——，而是信仰本身就是神悦纳的根据，因此这种悦纳就把永恒至福赐给那些信基督的人，而他们其实从来就不可能配得上它。

en: This difference in what is supposed to be the highest commandment for man leads to several consequences, or rather it is built on some important preceding propositions: namely, through all striving, through all sincere zeal for the good, man, on account of his complete incapacity for morality, can never bring it so far as to deserve happiness; whatever degree of it falls to his share he has from the undeserved free grace of God; from its justice he would have nothing to expect but misfortune and punishment.
Here the proposition is incontrovertibly laid at the foundation: the good man deserves happiness, he can demand it as a right, he is worthy of it.
Only, the impossibility of becoming a good man is presupposed.
zh: 这种差别——在究竟什么才该是人的最高诫命这一点上的差别——引出好几个后果，或者说，它本来就建立在前面几条重要的命题之上：也就是说，人尽管有一切努力、一切向善的真诚热忱，却由于自己完全无力做到道德，永远也走不到配得幸福的那一步；他能分到多少幸福，全凭上帝白白赐予、并不配得的恩典；若按它的公正来算，他除了不幸和惩罚再没有别的可指望。
这里不容反驳地被当作根据的正是这样一条命题：好人配得幸福，他可以把幸福当作权利来要求，他是配得上幸福的。
只不过，成为好人这件事被预先设定为不可能。

en: People have set Socrates, so many virtuous heathens, so many whole innocent peoples against these propositions until it became tedious, but always got the wretched answer which is outrageous to the man of feeling who believes in virtue, which a heartless church father hatched out and which equally empty disciples chattered after him until one is sick of it –: these had been only glittering vices.

That proposition which is so deeply grounded in the general moral nature of man – that the good man is worthy of happiness, a principle that expresses itself generally in the way sound common sense judges – the theologians themselves lay at the foundation in their doctrine of justice, but it is a proposition that still costs them trouble, which they seek to conceal, do not quite want to admit, for it is somewhat contrary to their fundamental doctrine of the suffering and death of Christ that satisfies [God].
zh: 人们一遍又一遍地拿苏格拉底、那么多有美德的异教徒、那么多整个清白无辜的民族来反驳这些命题，一直反驳到叫人厌烦，可得到的始终是那个可怜的回答——对一个相信美德、有感情的人来说，这回答简直令人愤慨——那是某个没心肝的教父炮制出来的，又被同样空洞的弟子们鹦鹉学舌地重复到令人恶心：这些只不过是光彩夺目的恶习罢了。
那条深深扎根于人的普遍道德本性之中的命题——好人配得幸福，这条原理在健全常识的判断方式里到处都有表现——神学家们在讲公正的学说时自己也把它当作根据；可这又是一条让他们为难的命题，他们设法把它藏起来，并不真的愿意承认，因为它跟他们那条关于基督代受苦难、代死以补赎的基本教义多少有些抵触。

en: The proposition of the depravity not only of men but of human nature – to which experience contradicts wherever bad governments have not degraded mankind – would not have been asserted and so elaborated merely through the weak exegesis of a few disconnected passages of Scripture that seemed to say this, if it did not have such great importance in the connection of the whole.

For this depravity and the aversion to the good, towards which reason is said to feel an insurmountable disgust, people have even believed they found the physical cause in Holy Scripture, and did not consider that through this propagation, in which the will of man can absolutely have no influence, according to which children already are declared worthy of punishment – that thereby man, who is besides supposed to stand under the influences of evil spirits, is straightway declared free of all guilt, that imputation can by no means take place where there is no practical freedom, where the capacity is denied him partly to recognise the good as such, partly to respect it, partly to give it preponderance over sensuousness.

Quite consistently, therefore, the heathens have been damned without grace and mercy, and the humane sentiment of those theologians who nowadays no longer dare to speak so flatly about it stands in contradiction with the rest of their system.
zh: 那条讲败坏的命题——不只是人的败坏，而是人性的败坏——只要没有糟糕的政府把人贬低，经验就同它相矛盾——倘若它在整个关联中没有那么大的重要性，单靠对《圣经》里几处似乎这样说的、彼此不相连的段落的浅薄解释，是不会被主张、更不会被阐发成这个样子的。

对于这种败坏，以及对于理性据说对善抱有的那种不可克服的厌恶，人们甚至以为在《圣经》里找到了它的自然原因，却没有想到：靠这种遗传——在遗传里人的意志根本不可能有任何影响，而按它说来连孩子都被宣布为该受惩罚的了——恰恰等于宣布人完全无罪，何况他还该是处在恶的精神的影响之下的；在没有实践自由的地方，在他被剥夺了下述能力的地方——既不能承认善之为善，也不能敬重善，更不能让善对感性取得优势——根本谈不上归罪。
所以，异教徒被毫无恩典和慈悲地判入永罚，这是完全一贯的做法；而那些如今再也不敢把话说得这么直白的神学家，他们那副仁厚的信念跟他们体系里的其余部分正相矛盾。

en: Since morality cannot now be made the supreme condition of bliss, because men are not capable of it, and bliss thus could not take place at all, another ingredient, of which man is still capable, has been substituted for it (put in its place) by the merciful grace of God – namely faith in Christ.

However necessary a component of faith one may require its activity in good works to be, yet according to the theologians' verdict there lies in the latter, for one thing, not that which could be meritorious for us, could give us a peculiar worth, could draw God's good pleasure upon us – and then faith in general depends on a conviction of the understanding or of the imagination, which are to hold things for true that rest partly on historical credibility, partly are of such a kind that the understanding cannot reconcile itself with them.
zh: 既然道德不能被当作至福的最高条件，因为人没有能力做到道德，而至福这样一来就根本无从谈起，那么，上帝那慈悲的恩典就另换了一种人还有能力办到的成分来代替它（放在它的位置上）——也就是对基督的信仰。
人们尽可以把信仰在善行中的活动说成信仰多么不可缺少的组成部分，但按神学家的说法，善行里首先并没有那种能让我们有功劳、能给我们一种独特的价值、能把神的悦纳引到我们身上来的东西；其次，信仰归根到底取决于知性或想象力的某种确信，即把一些事情信以为真，而这些事情一部分靠历史的可信性，一部分则属于知性根本无法与它们相容的那一类。

en: Faith in Christ as a historical person is not a faith grounded in a practical need of reason, but a faith that rests on the testimonies of others.

What has interest for reason, what sets a highest final end for man's existence and activity, what makes the keystone of the whole system of his tranquillity, of the solution of the questions important to him, has, according to what reason tells us about this, its
zh: 把基督当作一个历史人物来信仰，这种信仰并不是建立在实践理性的需要之中，而是建立在别人的证词之上。
凡是对理性有意义的东西，凡是为人的定在和活动设定一个最高终极目的的东西，凡是构成他安心的一整套体系、构成对他重要的问题之解决的拱心石的东西，按理性在这方面告诉我们的，都有它的

en: principle, its foundation in reason itself, whose development is only necessary in order to give every man the solution of those problems, and the access to it is therefore open to everyone who will hear its voice (one day tells it to another, etc.).

Historical faith, by contrast, is by its nature limited, its spread depends on contingent circumstances, it is a spring from which not everyone can draw – and yet the condition of God's good pleasure in us, of our fate for eternity, is supposed to depend on it.

One may here put on as modest and humble an air as one likes about our ignorance regarding the ways and intentions of providence, whose track people claim in other cases to have hit upon so exactly – we cannot ask why has nature denied to the animals the talents of man, the dispositions to reason and morality? – but if a wretched pride, which given the assumed depravity of our nature could support itself on nothing but that very depravity, will not place us in the rank of beings on a higher level than so countless other nations, then we may expect that the means, the school to a perfection that alone can give man worth, stand open to the whole human race.

And only two cases are possible: either the greater part of the human race was excluded from the blessing that drips through that faith upon us elect, upon us whose depravity, by our own admission, was at least equal to the depravity of the rest of the human race and therefore deserved nothing better – in which case we deny to our reason and to the general human feeling the concepts, so important, of the worthiness to be happy, which rests on the ethical, and cancel and deny the moral relation of the Godhead to the world and to men, the concept of its justice, for the sake of which alone its existence has any interest for us, and deny that the moral properties of God are in any degree knowable or determinable for us, that we can form any concept of his moral nature – of his manner of judging men, of what virtue is in his eyes – although we are supposed to learn so many transcendental and entirely mysterious properties of his from the Christian religion – either we must renounce it entirely, or we must admit that that faith is not of the enormous importance that is made out of it, not the single exclusive condition under which men can grasp something of their final end in the world, under which they can have a worth before God and reason.
zh: 原则，它的根基就在理性自身之中，只要把理性展开，就足以让每一个人得到那些问题的解答，而通往它的路对每个愿意听它声音的人都是敞开的（一天告诉另一天，等等）。
相反，历史性的信仰按其本性是受限的，它传播得广不广要看偶然的情况，它是一口并非人人都能从中汲水的泉源——可偏偏神对我们的悦纳、我们永恒的命运，其条件据说就取决于它。

在这件事上，人们尽可以对我们在护佑的道路和意图方面的无知表现得要多谦虚、多恭顺就多谦虚、多恭敬——对护佑，人们在别的场合却硬说自己是跟得那么准的——我们不能问：自然为什么把人的才能、把理性和道德的禀赋扣住不给动物？——可是，假如有一种可怜的高傲，它在我们本性败坏这个前提下除了败坏本身再也找不到别的东西可以依靠，却不愿在万物的等级里把我们摆到比数不清的其他民族更高的一层上，那么我们就有理由期待：那通向完善——唯有完善才能给人价值——的手段和学校，是对整个人类敞开的。

而且只有两种情况：要么人类中较大的那一部分被排除在那种福分之外——那福分是靠着那种信仰滴到我们这些被拣选者身上的，而按我们自己承认，我们的败坏至少和人类其余部分的败坏一样，因此也不配得到更好的东西——在那种情况下，我们就得对理性、对普遍的人类情感否认那个极其重要的概念，即配得幸福的概念（它建立在伦理之上），就得取消并否认神对世界和人的道德关系、否认神的公正这一概念（我们之所以对神的存在有兴趣，全是为了这个概念），否认神的道德属性在某种程度上对我们是可以认识、可以规定的，否认我们能对神的道德本性形成任何概念——对神如何审判人、在神眼里什么是美德——尽管我们据说还要从基督教里认识神那么多先验的、完全神秘的属性；要么我们就得承认，那种信仰并没有人们给它安上的那种巨大重要性，并不是那唯一的、排他性的条件，不是人借以能对自己在世上的终极目的有所领会、能面对神和理性具有价值的唯一条件。

en: The grounds of faith in Christ rest on history.

If simplicity of morals has still preserved a people from the great inequality of estates, and the history has taken place on the people's own soil, then the legends pass on from parents to children, they are in equal measure everyone's property; but as soon as particular estates form in a nation, and the father of the family is no longer at the same time high priest, an estate will soon come forward that is the depositary of the legends, from which the knowledge of them then spreads among the people; this will especially be the case when the legends have sprung up in a foreign land, among foreign customs, in a foreign language.

Here the ground, the content of the legends in its original form can no longer be the property of all, since, in order to become acquainted with that form, much time and a manifold apparatus of knowledge is required; in this way that estate will soon attain a dominion over public faith, which can expand into a very extensive power, or at least always keeps the reins in its hands with regard to the doctrines of the folk religion.
zh: 信仰基督的根据建立在历史上。
如果一个民族还靠着风俗的淳朴而没有被等级之间的巨大不平等沾染，历史又是在这个民族自己的土地上发生的，那么传说就会从父母传到子女，它们在同等程度上是每个人自己的财产；可是一旦一个民族里形成了特殊的等级，家长不再同时是最高祭司，很快就会有一个等级冒出来，成为这些传说的存放者，关于它们的知识再从它那里流传到民众中去；如果这些传说原本是在异乡、在异乡的风俗、异乡的语言里产生的，情形就尤其如此。
在这里，传说的根据、传说的内容以其原本的形式不再可能为所有人所有，因为要认识那种形式，需要很多时间和一整套各式各样的知识；这样一来，那个等级不久就会取得对公共信仰的支配权，这种支配可以扩展成一种范围极广的权力，或者至少总在民间宗教的教义方面把缰绳攥在自己手里。

en: Faith33) in what people tell us who possess our trust or are privileged by the state to be believed, is an infinitely more comfortable matter than accustoming oneself to reflection; historical faith is indeed capable of occasioning investigations, but it does not lie immediately in its nature to awaken the spirit of reflection; with moral rules or rules of prudence everyone believes himself entitled and finds himself moved to hold them together with his feeling and with his experiences and to judge of their truth and applicability.

In the case of historical truths the people is accustomed to believe what has been told it from youth on, and never to fall into doubt about it, and is condemned never to be able to enter into investigations about their truth.

Since the ground of our bliss is not supposed to rest on what our reason, attention to ourselves and others, our own thinking would be capable of examining, but on the authority of those to whom the state has chiefly entrusted the care for propagating historical truths, one can perhaps say that it lies in the nature of the matter that the use and cultivation of the understanding, trust in one's own insights, independence in one's convictions is so little promoted by it and is so little general.
zh: 相信33)那些我们所信任的人、或者国家特许我们可以相信的人对我们说的话，是一件比让自己养成思考习惯要舒服无数倍的事；历史性的信仰也能引起一番研究，但唤起思考的精神并不直接是它的本性；而对于道德的规矩或精明的规矩，每个人都认为自己有权、也觉得自己有必要把它们跟自己的感受和经验摆在一起，去判断它们是否真实、是否可用。
在历史真理方面，民众习惯于相信从小听来的东西，从不对它起疑，并且注定永远无法去研究它们是否真实。
既然我们至福的根据不应建立在我们的理性、对自己和对他人的留意、我们自己的思考所能检验的东西上，而应建立在那些人的权威上——国家主要就是把传播历史真理的事托付给了他们——那么也许可以说，事情本身就决定了：知性的运用和培养、对自己洞见的信任、在信念上的独立自主，靠它是很少得到促进的，也是很少普及的。

en: Faith – this faith differs further from the historical one by its higher degree of liveliness, a tension of the soul, and is in the end still exposed to fate; however much it may be surrounded by authority, however finely and artificially the circumstances may be combined into a system that one can nowhere get at without having to entangle oneself in an endless detail in order to remove all hypotheses, all possibilities – in the end reason still dares to examine that faith out of itself, to draw out of itself the principles of possibility and probability, regardless of that artificial historical edifice, which it leaves lying on one side and [which] asserts a primacy over the conviction of rational truths on historical grounds.
zh: 信仰——这种信仰与历史性的信仰还有一点不同，就是它的生动程度更高，是灵魂的一种紧张，而且归根到底仍然听凭命运的摆布；它周围尽可以布满权威，种种情况尽可以被精细而人为地组合成一个体系，让人无论如何也碰不到它，除非陷进没完没了的细节里去，把一切假设、一切可能都排除掉——可到最后，理性还是敢从自身出发去检验那种信仰，从自身出发去汲取可能性和或然性的原则，而不管那座人为的历史大厦；理性把它撂在一边，而它却硬说自己对出于历史理由的理性真理之确信具有优先地位。

en: Once reason has been brought up so far that it feels this autonomy of its own, then its conviction, drawn from itself and grounded in itself, has such strength that it either pays no attention at all to that historical faith and its proofs, is wholly unconcerned about it, and draws upon itself the reproach of a criminal frivolity; or if people do not cease to hold that faith before its eyes and to storm it with it, and it does not understand how to attack this faith in itself also on historical grounds, if it lacks the erudition for that and therefore stubbornly refuses to surrender, then it is accused of deliberate blindness; or it seeks either itself to shake the historical faith through wit, through the representation of the absurdity of many a narrative, or [through this,] that it treats the sacred history like any other human work and presupposes with regard to its legends the possibility of having been altered or of having had its ground merely in a folk belief, just as with the traditions of other peoples – or that it attacks the historical faith with its own weapons and does not find in the books that make up its foundation what it draws out of them, and seeks to accommodate the same in every possible way – in this case it is accused of lack of respect for the divine word, of malice and dishonesty.
zh: 理性一旦被养到这样大，以致感觉到自己这种自律，那么它那从自身汲取、在自身中有根据的确信就有这样一种力量：它要么根本不理会那种历史性的信仰及其论据，对之全不放在心上，因而给自己招来一个罪名——该受责备的轻浮草率；要么人们如果不停地把它那种信仰摆到理性眼前、拿它来围攻理性，而理性又不懂得从自身出发也以历史的理由去攻击这种信仰，如果它缺少这方面的学问，因而顽固地拒绝交出阵地，那它就被指为蓄意盲目；要么它设法自己去动摇历史性的信仰，靠机智，靠表象出某些叙述的荒谬，或者靠把神圣历史当成另一部人的作品来处理，对它的传说也像对其他民族的传统那样，预设它们可能被改动过，或者本来就只是建立在一种民众信仰之上；要么它用历史性信仰自己的武器来攻击它，在构成其根据的那些书里找不到它从书里引出来的东西，并想方设法去迁就它——无论哪种情况，它都被指责为不尊重神的话，是恶毒和不诚实。

en: Faith in Christ is faith in a personified ideal (see p. 81 ff.).
zh: 对基督的信仰，是对一个被人格化了的理想的信仰（参看第81页及以下）。

en: Why do examples of human beings not suffice to strengthen us in the struggle of virtue, to feel the divine spark in us, the power that lies in us, to become master over the sensuous?

Why do we not recognise in virtuous human beings that they are not only flesh of our flesh, bone of our bone, but also feel the moral sympathy, that this is spirit of our spirit, power of our power? - Ah, we have been persuaded that these capacities are foreign, that man belongs only in the series of natural beings, and indeed of corrupted ones; the idea of holiness has been utterly isolated and ascribed solely to a distant being, it has been held incompatible with the limitation under a sensuous nature; - if therefore moral perfection could be attributed to this being, it would not make up a part of our own essence, but only through the union of that being of all beings itself with us, through its dwelling in us (unio mystica), could its working in us be possible.
This debasing of human nature therefore does not allow us to recognise ourselves in virtuous human beings, - for such an ideal, which would be an image of virtue for us, a God-man was needed.

It is still well for us if we find the truly divine in him, not precisely in this, that he is the second person of the Godhead, that he is begotten of the Father from eternity etc., but in this, that his spirit, his disposition agreed with the moral law, whose idea we must, to be sure, in the end fetch out of ourselves, even if its letter can be given in signs and words.

But that this true divine in it has often been misjudged and set aside is shown, on the one hand, by the disputes, often unto life and death, of the scholars and the priests - that is, of those whose duty it was to keep attention on those moral properties - over predicates so barren for morality as the eternal generation, the manner of the union of the divine with the human, etc., about which unessential properties one finds in school-correct compendia the most exhaustive determinations, which in the end become so fine that they slip away from one between the fingers.

The various opinions about this have been made into essential affairs of religion, they have not stayed in the studies, but the people and the governments have been called upon to take part, in order to use their power against the party that thinks otherwise and to let it atone for its errors in its blood or in prison.
In this way the essential thing about the ideal has evidently been overlooked, misjudged - the property on account of which it was to be ideal, divine, for us.

But no less do other, equally sad experiences show us that this was not the only possible way of misjudging it, that human beings could still cling to even more unessential properties of it, could sacrifice their own and others' blood for them, for its mere name, for words that were joined to it or that came from it (p. 85).

But by what arrangements it could be brought about that in Christ not merely the human being, not merely his name, but virtue itself be recognised and loved - the answering of this question rests on the solution of the problem of how a people can be brought up at all to receptivity for moral ideas and to morality, a problem whose execution would be too far-reaching for our purpose and of which the object of our consideration is merely the share that the Christian religion wants to take in it incidentally through the detours of its faith.

But the hinge on which the whole hope of our bliss turns is faith in Christ as the reconciler of God with the world, as the one who in our place bore the punishments that the human race had deserved, partly because of its natural corruption, partly by its own fault, which sufferings of an innocent one - for he was God - are to be deducted from the immeasurable debt of the human race and credited to us for our benefit. - Against this storey in the building of the Christian faith the other doctrines are to be taken only as so many supporting buttresses; therefore it was necessary to assert the worthlessness of human beings and their incapacity ever to attain a worth by nature, [to assert] the doctrine of the divinity of Christ - for only the suffering of such a one could counterbalance the debt of the human race -, therefore [also] to work out the doctrine of the free grace of God, because that history, to which our bliss is bound, could remain unknown to half the world through no fault of its own, and so many others that hang together with it.

Even if one thereby removes the insipid representation that Christ in fact himself endured in his sufferings the punishment of the whole world, by saying simply and in general that God has attached the forgiveness of our sins to these sufferings, that they were the condition of the return of his grace, which man of course cannot comprehend from his moral relation to the Godhead and by which the above absurdity is not helped out so very much, there still remains the main thought: on account of another's merit human beings are forgiven their debt, if only they will believe this.
zh: 为什么人的榜样还不足以让我们在美德的斗争中坚强起来，不足以让我们感觉到心中那神圣的火花、我们自身中那股力量，凭它去成为感性的主人？

为什么我们在有美德的人身上看不到，他们不只是我们骨中的骨、肉中的肉，而且还感觉到那种道德上的同感，即这是我们的精神所出的精神、我们的力量所出的力量？——唉，有人劝服了我们，说这些能力是外来的，说人只属于自然存在物的行列，而且是其中败坏的那一类；人们把神圣性的观念完全孤立起来，单单归给一个遥远的本质，认为它跟感性自然之下的那种限制根本无法相容；——所以，如果可以把道德上的完善归给这个本质，那它就不成其为我们自己本质的一部分，而只有通过那一切本质之本质本身与我们相结合，通过它寓居于我们之中（unio mystica），它在我们之中的作用才成为可能。
这种对人性的贬低，于是就不许我们在有美德的人身上重新认出我们自己；——要有一个能给我们充当美德之形象的理想，就需要一位神人。
如果我们在他身上找到那真正神圣的东西，我们还算有福——不是在他乃神性的第二位格、他自永恒以来为父所生等等之中找到，而是在他的精神、他的信念与道德法则相一致之中找到；这法则的观念，我们归根到底当然还得从我们自己这里取来，哪怕它的字句可以用符号和词语给出。
不过，这个真正的神圣东西在其中常常被认错、被搁到一边，这方面一来看学者和教士们那些往往拼到你死我活的争论——也就是说，那些人的义务本是让人始终关注那些道德品质——争的是永恒受生、神性与人性结合的方式等等对道德如此没有结果的谓词；关于这些无关紧要的属性，人们在合乎学派的教本里找得到最详尽的界定，而这些界定到最后细得能从指缝里溜走。
关于这些问题的各种意见被弄成了宗教的要紧事务；它们没有留在书房里，而是号召民众、号召政府一起来参与，好对想法不同的一派动用权力，让那一派用自己的血或者在牢里为自己的错误赎罪。
在这条路上，理想中要紧的东西显然被看漏了、认错了——就是那种属性，凭它这理想才该对我们成为理想、成为神圣。
但同样可悲的其他经验也告诉我们，这并不是认错它唯一可能的方式：人们还会死死抓住它那些更无关紧要的属性，为这些属性、为它单纯的名字、为与它连在一起或者由它而来的那些词句，牺牲自己和别人的血（第85页）。
但要通过哪些安排才能做到：在基督身上被认识和被爱的不是单纯的人、不是单纯他的名字，而是美德本身——这个问题的回答取决于另一个问题的解决，即一个民族究竟怎样才能被培养得对道德观念有接受能力、并且有道德；这个问题要真做起来，对我们的意图来说铺得太远，我们要考察的只是：基督宗教借它信仰上的那些绕弯的路，顺便想在这件事上占一份。

但是，我们整个至福希望所绕着的那个轴心，就是信仰基督是神与世界的和解者，是代替我们承担了那些刑罚的那一位——人类因自己本性的败坏，也因自己招来的罪过，该受那些刑罚；而一个无辜者的这些苦难——因为他就是神——要从人类那无法度量的罪债里勾销，并算在我们的账上、为我们所用。——对基督信仰这座建筑的这一层，其他学说只能看作许多起支撑作用的扶壁；所以就有必要主张人的一文不值和他凭本性永远不可能获得价值的无能，有必要阐发基督神性的学说——因为只有一个这样的人的受难才抵得过人类的罪债——，也有必要阐发神自由施恩的学说，因为那桩与我们的至福绑在一起的历史，世界上有一半人可能毫无过错地始终不知道，此外还要阐发与之相连的许多别的学说。
即使人们借此把那套乏味的表象——基督在他的苦难里确实亲自受尽了全世界的刑罚——去掉，办法只是笼统地说：神把赦免我们的罪系于这些苦难，这些苦难是他重新施恩的条件——这一点，人当然无法从他与神的那种道德关系里去以概念把握，而上头那个荒唐的说法也并没因此被补救多少——，那么剩下的还是那个主要念头：由于别人的功绩，人们的罪债被免除，只要他们愿意相信这一点。
